binutils/readelf.c numeric GNU build attribute parsing block

descriptions: A length derived from an input note name field controls a numeric decode loop without first being bounded to the capacity of the destination integer. Oversized bytes values let untrusted name data continue through shift-based numeric accumulation beyond the intended value width. The patch blocks this by checking bytes against sizeof (val), reporting a corrupt name field, and returning FALSE before the loop.

suggestions: First-draft detector should anchor on bytes derived from pnote->namesz - (name - pnote->namedata) and then used as the while (bytes --) loop bound.
Treat the missing guard bytes > sizeof (val) before the loop as the main vulnerability condition, but do not require the exact error(...) text for initial matching.
Track local data flow from pnote->namesz into bytes and from bytes into the decode loop; interprocedural or cross-file analysis is not needed for this patch.
Use the shift/accumulation loop and *name++ consumption as stronger anchors than the later printf formatting changes.
Use printf format changes only as secondary convergence evidence, not as the primary sink.
